summary: S-3 meets C-7. src/server.mjs now exports createApp(store), which replaces the '0 notes' placeholder in public/index.html with store.length followed by ' notes' for GET /. The new tests/server.test.mjs (untracked) asserts '0 notes' for an empty store and '3 notes' for a store of three created notes, both through the real HTTP handler. npm test ran 9 tests: 9 pass, 0 fail, exit 0. The slice touches only paths listed for S-3 (src/server.mjs, tests/server.test.mjs); public/ is unchanged and the existing placeholder already matches. One major finding: the standalone entry point always serves createApp([]), so the running page (npm start, the fixture devServer) can only ever show '0 notes'. The criterion is met as written because N is the store length, but the count is not observable end to end on the running server. No block findings.

findings.issue: The standalone entry point starts the server with createApp([]), a fresh empty array that nothing else can populate. The live page therefore always shows '0 notes' regardless of how many notes exist in any process, so C-7 is only verified through the test harness and not on the running app. This is a behavior risk for the dev server and any deployed page, not a failure of the literal criterion, which ties N to the store passed in.
findings.suggestion: Before handoff, decide how the running server gets its store (shared module-level store, or a note of the limitation in the handoff). Not required to satisfy C-7 as written.

findings.issue: The count text is always '<N> notes', so a store of exactly one note renders '1 notes'. C-7 and the handoff literally ask for 'N notes', so this is met, but the wording is ungrammatical for N=1.
findings.suggestion: Optional: render '1 note' for a single note if the handoff wording allows it. Keep 'N notes' otherwise.
